title: Pattern cards: the owner's eleven problem patterns from a retail interview, each with its recipe and practice questions
request: Phase 8, Part C (the owner): better and real business examples with a lot of knowledge the agents can use, from the problems a retail group's AI lead described in an interview.
plan: Transcribe the owner's eleven problem cards into the knowledge base's v2 shape: what was said, the general problem, why it is hard, how to solve and measure it, the common mistakes, the same problem in other industries.
Link each pattern to the recipe it maps to: built today, planned in a named package, or knowledge only.
Attach the ten practice questions to their patterns and measure whether the search finds each question's own pattern.

decisions.decision: The patterns are written without anyone's name, internal tool name or brand, and the conversation itself is kept only in the field a model never reads.
decisions.why: The owner decided that a model reads patterns, not people; the raw transcript stays in the owner's own folder.

decisions.decision: The common mistakes go into the example's pitfalls, where every role already looks, rather than a second list.
decisions.why: The roles and the replicas already read pitfalls; one list avoids two copies of the same text.

decisions.decision: The cross-industry cases are kept on each pattern, not as separate thin examples.
decisions.why: A case of one line has nothing a role can use on its own; on the pattern it lets a person's words from another industry find the pattern.

change: dclab_rnd/knowledge/retail_interview_patterns.json (the eleven patterns, the ten practice questions, the owner's rubric); dclab_core.business_examples.practice_recall (dclab-core 0.77.0); dclab_rnd/business_examples.py (from_owner_documents, --practice); tests/test_business_examples.py (PatternCardTests); evidence/business_examples rebuilt.

findings.defect: The cross-industry table was incomplete and misfiled.
findings.scenario: Filtering the patterns by industry, healthcare and travel never showed the department agents, nor logistics the near-duplicates.
findings.cause: Two industries were renamed in transcription and one row of the owner's table was left out.
findings.fix: The table's cases filed under the owner's seven industries, the missing one added; a test that patterns 1, 4, 6 and 8 cover all seven.

findings.defect: Pattern 9 lost the owner's example for each rung of the ladder.
findings.scenario: Practice question 8 (invoices, emails, demand planning) is answered by those examples, and the card no longer held them.
findings.cause: The examples column of the owner's table was not transcribed.
findings.fix: Each rung carries its example (moving data between systems, standard supplier invoices, churn and demand, ticket routing, contract review).

findings.defect: Pattern 3 lost the audit sample and the label source of the owner's cascade.
findings.scenario: 30.17 builds that cascade from the card, which never said each review batch carries a random audit sample.
findings.cause: The diagram's fifth and sixth stages were summarised away.
findings.fix: The card says every reviewed case keeps its source, every batch carries a random audit sample, and the trained model becomes the new first stage.

findings.defect: The practice questions' criteria were the transcriber's, filed as the owner's.
findings.scenario: A grader in 30.18 would judge answers by criteria the owner did not write; four questions named no split or baseline.
findings.cause: The owner's one rubric (the metric, the validation split, the first simple baseline) was replaced by per-question picks.
findings.fix: The owner's rubric heads every question's list, and the note says the rest is derived from the card.

findings.defect: The recipe-link test passed with a misspelt kind or a missing replica.
findings.scenario: A pattern marked built with a kind that does not exist, or naming a replica no module provides, passed.
findings.cause: The test checked only that a planned package appears in the plan.
findings.fix: Built kinds must be in the registry, planned ones name a new kind or modifiers, knowledge links carry none, and every replica named exists.

findings.defect: The name test checked nothing in the gate and never checked brands or tools.
findings.scenario: In the gate's clean worktree the owner's folder is absent, so the test read no names and a brand put into a field passed.
findings.cause: The names were read from a folder outside the repository.
findings.fix: The test hashes every word and pair of words of the patterns against committed hashes of the forbidden names, brands and tools, and checks every pattern's conversation stays out of a model's context.

findings.defect: The knowledge base's evaluation lived where the main product cannot import it.
findings.scenario: The main product could not measure its own examples the same way.
findings.cause: practice_recall was written in the studio's package.
findings.fix: practice_recall moved into dclab_core (0.77.0), with its integration note.

findings.defect: Wording departed from the owner's document.
findings.scenario: Five patterns the owner calls industry-free were filed under retail; a near-duplicate case was shown as a mistake; data-residency laws were limited to governments.
findings.cause: Transcription choices made without checking the source page.
findings.fix: Industry left empty for those five, the case moved to the other industries, the laws applied to any company, the review capacity in the owner's words.

measurements.name: practice questions against the search (30.8)
measurements.gate: every practice question finds its own pattern among the first three of every example (the plan's Done when)
measurements.result: 10 of 10 practice questions rank their own pattern first among 49 examples (4 research tracks, 17 replicas, 1 owner solution, 11 patterns, 16 written); the questions are not in the index
measurements.against_gate: Met: every question finds its own pattern, each at rank 1.
limits: The owner wrote the questions and the patterns from the same cards: they share words, so this is an easy test; paraphrases by an independent writer come with the package where roles read the examples.
A search that finds the pattern does not show that a role reading it decides better: that is measured on the journeys.

outcome: The knowledge base holds the owner's eleven patterns as examples a role may read, each with its recipe link and practice questions, and the search finds each question's pattern first.
lessons: A knowledge base needs its own evaluation questions kept out of its index, or the search measures itself.
Transcribing a document is a measurement too: each field is checked against its page, and a test pins what the transcriber must not change.
risks: Four patterns (7, 8, 10 and 11) are knowledge only until Part G builds them.
The practice measurement is optimistic by construction (one author).
